findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded directly in the function's environment variables, exposing them in the Terraform source, the state file, and to any principal able to call lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration. The function already has an execution role, so static keys are both unnecessary and a persistent, non-rotatable credential leak.

No kms_key_arn is configured, so environment variables containing secrets are protected only by the default AWS-managed Lambda key and are returned in cleartext by the GetFunctionConfiguration API to any caller with that permission. A customer-managed CMK would add a separate key-policy authorisation boundary around these sensitive values.

The function targets the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of support and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the runtime and its bundled libraries unremediated.

The function has no vpc_config block, so it executes in the Lambda-managed public network with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or subnet controls. Combined with the embedded static credentials, this removes any network-layer barrier to exfiltrating those secrets or reaching arbitrary external endpoints.
